notes: DRAFT for scholarly review; nothing here is reviewed or published. English only: Arabic and Urdu are left for translators. Written from the Quran text in content/quran (Tanzil Uthmani) in the drafter's own words, and from nothing else: no hadith, no tafsir, no later tradition in the story texts. Chapters are a reading order, not a chronology the Quran claims. Where the Quran leaves a person unnamed or names only a title, the draft keeps them unnamed; identifications and later-tradition names appear only in the unknowns and uncertainties. Honorifics are added when the page is rendered.

claims.statement_en: God wished to show Fir'awn, Haman and their forces, through those who were weakened, what they feared.
The family of Fir'awn picked up the child, so that he would become an enemy and a source of grief to them, and Fir'awn, Haman and their forces were in error.

chapters.summary_md: God wished to show Fir'awn, Haman and their forces what they feared [c1]. The ayah names Haman among those who were in error when the family of Fir'awn picked up the child [c2].
chapters.body_md: God wished to show Fir'awn, Haman and their forces, through those who were weakened, what they feared [c1]. The family of Fir'awn picked up the child, so that he would become an enemy and a source of grief to them, and Fir'awn, Haman and their forces were in error [c2].
chapters.deep_md: In both ayat Haman is named after Fir'awn and before the forces [c1][c2]. The ayat do not give his office, and they do not say what he did [c1].
chapters.kids_md: The Quran names Haman beside Fir'awn and their forces [c1][c2]. God wished to show them what they feared [c1].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the Quran names Haman among those who were in error [c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: Haman's office, his origin or his time.
- Not established: what Haman did in these events.
- Not established: what they feared, beyond the words of the ayah.

claims.statement_en: Fir'awn told Haman to light a fire on clay and make him a lofty tower, so that he might climb up to the god of Musa, and said that he thought Musa a liar.
Fir'awn told Haman to build him a tower so that he might reach the ways, the ways of the heavens, and look at the god of Musa, and said that he thought Musa a liar.

chapters.summary_md: Fir'awn told Haman to build him a lofty tower so that he might climb up to the god of Musa [c1][c2]. He said that he thought Musa a liar [c1].
chapters.body_md: Fir'awn told Haman to light a fire on clay and make him a lofty tower, so that he might climb up to the god of Musa, and said that he thought Musa a liar [c1]. Fir'awn told Haman to build him a tower so that he might reach the ways, the ways of the heavens, and look at the god of Musa, and said that he thought Musa a liar [c2].
chapters.deep_md: One passage tells Haman to light a fire on clay and the other to build [c1][c2]. Neither says whether Haman did it or whether the tower was finished [c2].
chapters.kids_md: Fir'awn told Haman to build him a lofty tower [c1]. He wanted to climb up to the god of Musa [c1].
chapters.lessons_md: Educational interpretation (not scripture): One reading is that the passages record an order given to Haman and not his answer [c1][c2].
chapters.unknowns_md:
- Not established: whether Haman built the tower, or how he answered.
- Not established: what became of Haman.

uncertainties_en: Named in later tradition, not in the Quranic text: Haman is described as Fir'awn's minister or vizier, and later works discuss his origin and his end.
Whether Haman is a personal name or a title is not settled by the text.
Hadith to add later: reports about Haman, with a named grader for each; none is used here.
